thread:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: increased DNS errors for production-api.redwood.ai from EU regions (eu-west-1). Multiple customers reporting 5xx and DNS lookup failures. Paging on-call.
maria-g: seeing a surge of SERVFAIL and NXDOMAIN in proxy logs. Customer-facing 502s. Quick sample from proxy logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T11:21:18Z] upstream_dns: SERVFAIL for production-api.redwood.ai from resolver 1.1.1.1
[2026-03-15T11:21:22Z] proxy: 502 -> client=54.37.12.4 route=eu-west-1
```
leo-b: traces show geo-dns answers are inconsistent — some EU clients get us-east endpoints. I compared dig from two vantage points:
```
# dig @1.1.1.1 production-api.redwood.ai +short
52.12.34.56

# dig @9.9.9.9 production-api.redwood.ai +short
<empty>  ; NXDOMAIN
```
jamal: Route53 healthcheck flapping for eu pool around 11:20-11:23 UTC, weight briefly moved to global pool then back. Also Cloudflare resolvers returning cached answers with TTLs that mismatch what Route53 is serving.
andrea: @sre-oncall can you take? I'm on parental call, can assist with status page and customer comms.
sre-oncall: taking it. On-call: s-reed. Handoff: I'm going to follow the GeoDNS runbook (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/geo-dns-failovers). Immediate goal: stop bad route churn and restore consistent answers for eu clients.
eng-runtime: quick checks — KV cache on proxies looks ok. This looks network/authoritative side. netsim-bot: starting resolver probe sweep across CF/Route53/Google.
jamal: recommended immediate mitigations:
- disable Route53 weighted failover for eu pool (stop oscillation)
- promote eu-secondary static A records (low TTL) to active pool
- request Cloudflare to purge resolver cache for production-api.redwood.ai
sre-oncall: doing step 1 -> disabling automatic failover (console command):
```
# aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch file://freeze-eu-failover.json
```
Applied. Change ID: C0MPLETED123. Waiting for propagation (should be ~30s-2m for our config).
leo-b: initiating Cloudflare purge (using service token):
```
curl -s -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/<zone>/purge_cache" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CF_TOKEN}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"files":["https://production-api.redwood.ai/"]}'
```
Purge request queued; response id abc123.
maria-g: running live probes after Route53 freeze and CF purge:
```
# from eu-probe-1
dig @9.9.9.9 production-api.redwood.ai +short
52.12.34.56

# curl -v https://production-api.redwood.ai/health
* Connected to 52.12.34.56
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
Looks like answers stabilized for probe-1.
netsim-bot: Probe sweep results: 87% resolvers returning eu A record after mitigations. Earlier was ~55%.
andrea: updating status page: small subset of EU customers experiencing degraded API (5xx) — mitigation in progress. ETA 30m.
customer-signal (via sales): Customer AcmeCorp reported timeouts around 11:19-11:44 UTC, now reporting requests succeeding.
sre-oncall: monitoring metrics; 5xx rate dropped from 3.4% -> 0.3% over last 8 minutes. I'll keep the Route53 change frozen and leave CF purge in place for an hour.
leo-b: root cause hypothesis: a combination of Route53 healthcheck flapping + stale answers cached at external resolvers (Cloudflare & ISP resolvers) caused asymmetric routing where some clients hit an unready pool. TTLs were optimistic; our failover loop made small perturbations that amplified due to external cache behavior.
maria-g: for immediate RCA notes: impacted scope ~EU region, ~4 customers with visible errors, total user-facing error window ~25 minutes. No data loss. Postmortem owner: @leo-b to coordinate. Action items assigned:
- jamal: add jitter + debounce to Route53 failover automation (P0 change)
- leo-b: postmortem and timeline
- andrea: customer communications follow-ups
- eng-runtime: add resolver probe to alerting (detect >10% resolver divergence)
sre-oncall: marking incident mitigated — creating incident ticket INC-2026-042. Will keep monitoring for 2 hours and then close if stable. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
eng-runtime: quick note — we should consider lowering default TTLs for geo answers during failover windows and add an automated CF cache purge step in the failover runbook.
andrea: I'll draft status update to customers in #customer-updates and copy the timeline once leo posts the RCA.
leo-b: I'll own the postmortem, starting timeline capture now. Thanks team.
